correctness.summary: The multinomial mode equals Jefferson allocation; Janson's fixed-probability Jefferson seat-excess theorem is exactly a Cesaro limit over house size. Bounded seat excesses permit polynomial moment transfer. Combining Janson's marginal centered-uniform representation with the Bernoulli-polynomial generating function yields a factor p_i^(k+1), which cancels the p_i^(-k) coefficient weight after summing. Stirling-number coefficient extraction gives the stated universal formula.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Elezovic (2026) explicitly leaves on-slice modal Cesaro averaging open. Janson (2014) provides the Jefferson displacement limit but predates the multinomial coefficient family. Searches found no all-orders modal log-coefficient average or equivalent Bernoulli--Stirling universal formula. Older rounding and goodness-of-fit literature is acknowledged as prior machinery.

value.summary: The result closes the recent modal-averaging question to all logarithmic orders and reveals a probability-vector-independent constant at every order. It also gives a general polynomial-transfer principle for modal coefficients through the Jefferson limit law.

limitations: Fixed dimension and rationally independent probabilities only.
Cesaro convergence in the house size; no pointwise coefficient limit is claimed.
No quantitative convergence rate is proved.
The universal closed form is for individual logarithmic coefficients; multiplicative coefficients require the joint limit law.
Independent audit has not been performed.
